label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables.
unit: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables at the age of eleven to live as an adopted orphan with Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. She formed a deep bond of friendship with Diana Barry and developed an academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he angered her at school. Encouraged by her teacher Miss Stacy, Anne attended Queen's Academy, gained her teaching license, and later taught school in Avonlea and Valley Road while organizing the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. She pursued higher education at Redmond College alongside close friends Priscilla Grant and Philippa Gordon, living at Patty's Place. Eventually, she married Dr. Blythe, traveled to Europe for a medical congress, and became a mother of six children, residing at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye is an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye, an orphan, was taken in by his aunt, Mrs. George Pye, and attended the Avonlea school taught by Anne Shirley. From his arrival, he harbored a prejudice against Anne, believing she was no good like all girl teachers. He frequently engaged in classroom pranks, such as pouring water down Aurelia Clay's neck and placing a lively mouse inside Anne's desk drawer. Though Anne initially strove to win his affection without physical discipline, Anthony's repeated mockery and defiance eventually drove her to whip him with a pointer, causing him to cry.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea prior to her birth. Later in life, after her daughter Elizabeth married and moved to India as a foreign missionary, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. She agreed to move to Kingsport to act as housekeeper at Patty's Place for Anne, Priscilla, Phil, and Stella, quickly winning their deep affection. While managing Patty's Place, she kept house alongside three cats, including her bed-companion the Sarah-cat, whose purring comforted her worries about snakes in India. After the college girls completed their studies, she eventually traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field despite her dread of snakes.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews lived in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews lived in Avonlea and drove a double-seated buggy, taking guests like Anne Shirley and Diana Barry to a concert at White Sands. Immensely admiring Anne, he insisted that she sit next to him on the front seat during the drive. Later, after his father gave him the upper farm in his own name, Billy wished to marry Anne but was too shy to ask her directly. He persuaded his sister Jane to propose to Anne on his behalf. Following Anne's rejection, he did not break his heart and instead married Nettie Blewett. The couple made their first official appearance at church together to the pride and pleasure of the Andrews family.

label: History
value: Captain Jim was born James Boyd.
unit: Born James Boyd, Captain Jim spent his youth on Prince Edward Island listening to poetry recited by schoolmaster John Selwyn. Descended from seafarers, he ran off to sea as a boy and spent fifty years sailing across the globe. Over fifty years before meeting Anne Blythe, he lost his sweetheart Margaret in a sudden storm at sea, spending months searching the shore for her body in vain. During his travels he rescued an amnesiac named Dick Moore in Cuba and brought him back to his wife Leslie. Retiring from the sea, he became the lighthouse keeper at Four Winds Point, befriending his companion cat, the First Mate. He built close friendships with the residents of the area, including Anne Blythe, Gilbert Blythe, Cornelia Bryant, and Owen Ford, with whom he collaborated to write his life's stories in a book titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim. He passed away peacefully in his sleep shortly before the publication of his book.

He remains unbothered by bugs or slimy creatures, handling them with affectionate fascination.

label: History
value: Carl moves to Glen St. Mary
unit: Carl moves to Glen St. Mary when his father, John Meredith, becomes the minister of the Presbyterian church. He spends much of his time exploring the outdoors and collecting bugs, caterpillars, and spiders, which he frequently brings into the manse to the dismay of Aunt Martha and church visitors. Carl becomes a member of the Good Conduct Club formed by the Meredith and Blythe children to improve their behavior through self-imposed punishments. During one initiation dare, Carl eats a dead spider on a dare from his brother Jerry, which leads to a severe illness and pneumonia. The community rallies around the family, and Carl eventually recovers. When his father marries Rosemary West, Carl gains a loving stepmother who supports his interest in natural history, even building a box to house his pet toad.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth's real name is Leonora Bowman.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth, whose real name is Leonora Bowman, was hired at age fourteen to work for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, following in the footsteps of her three older sisters who had each served Miss Lavendar and then departed for Boston. Miss Lavendar continued calling her Charlotta to avoid confusion. Charlotta warmly welcomed visitors like Anne Shirley and Diana Barry to Echo Lodge, developing a deep admiration for Anne and secretly practicing her manners in her bedroom mirror. When Miss Lavendar became quiet and depressed, Charlotta expressed deep worry for her mistress's health and happiness. She assisted with the preparations for Miss Lavendar's marriage to Stephen Irving and subsequently moved with them to Boston, where she initially experienced severe homesickness. Over time, she blossomed into a young woman, gave up her iconic hair ribbons for a pompadour hairstyle, and married a good-tempered bricklayer named Tom. She returned to Prince Edward Island for visits during the summers and attended Anne Shirley's wedding, enthusiastically throwing rice and old shoes at the departing couple.

label: History
value: Cornelia grew up as an only child for eight years.
unit: Cornelia grew up as an only child for eight years until her younger brother was born. Although she had her pick of suitors when she was young, she remained unmarried for many years, nursing a long-standing disdain for men and Methodists while serving as a compassionate neighbor in Four Winds. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, she promptly formed a close friendship with her, frequently visiting to swap stories, sew, and mock local events. She also served as Leslie Moore's best friend, helping her through her hardships and cleaning the gray house up the brook. Cornelia was elected a delegate to the W.F.M.S. convention in Kingsport. Later, she accepted a proposal from Marshall Elliott, whom she married despite his Conservative political stance, remaining Mrs. Marshall Elliott for thirteen years by the time of Glen St. Mary events. When Mary Vance was discovered starving in a barn over-harbour, Cornelia sent her husband to investigate and took Mary into her home, where Mary became a helpful companion. Cornelia also participated actively in the Presbyterian church and Ladies' Aid Society, helping clean the manse and taking in the minister's children when needed.

label: History
value: Davy's mother died
unit: Following the death of his sick mother, Davy and his twin sister Dora were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. Unaccustomed to proper discipline in his early childhood, he caused constant distraction and mischief upon his arrival, such as locking his sister in a shed and ruining lemon pies by falling on them from a pantry shelf. Davy quickly formed a deep attachment to Anne Shirley, who helped guide his upbringing and morality. He began attending school, sitting beside Milty Boulter, though his unruly antics continued, including cutting up Dora's aprons, scaring Mrs. Rachel Lynde with a jack-o'-lantern, and chasing Mrs. Lynde's rooster until it died. He also ran away from Sunday School to go fishing with the Cotton boys. As he grew older, Davy reformed his rebellious tendencies and settled into a helpful, clever young boy. By his ninth year, he developed a strong passion for farming and sought permission from Marilla to run the Green Gables farm.

Unaccustomed to proper discipline in his early childhood, he caused constant distraction and mischief upon his arrival, such as locking his sister in a shed and ruining lemon pies by falling on them from a pantry shelf. Davy quickly formed a deep attachment to Anne Shirley, who helped guide his upbringing and morality. He began attending school, sitting beside Milty Boulter, though his unruly antics continued, including cutting up Dora's aprons, scaring Mrs. Rachel Lynde with a jack-o'-lantern, and chasing Mrs. Lynde's rooster until it died. He also ran away from Sunday School to go fishing with the Cotton boys. As he grew older, Davy reformed his rebellious tendencies and settled into a helpful, clever young boy. By his ninth year, he developed a strong passion for farming and sought permission from Marilla to run the Green Gables farm.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grows up at Orchard Slope.
unit: Diana Barry grows up at Orchard Slope as a close playmate and bosom friend of Anne Shirley, taking a solemn oath of eternal friendship with her in the garden. Although briefly forbidden by her strict mother from playing with Anne after an incident, their bond is restored after Anne saves Diana's sister Minnie May from croup. When the Avonlea Village Improvement Society is established, Diana serves as its treasurer. As she grows up, she enters a romance with Fred Wright, whom she eventually marries in a evening ceremony before moving away to their new home.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen area.
unit: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen area as the son of storekeeper Abner Moore. He pursued Leslie West persistently and married her when she was seventeen, but quickly grew restless with quiet married life. In the spring following his marriage, he went to Nova Scotia to visit relatives and joined his double cousin, George Moore, on a voyage to Havana on the vessel 'Four Sisters'. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died thirteen years prior to the events in Montreal. His cousin George stayed behind to nurse him while the vessel sailed, but Dick succumbed to the illness and was buried in Cuba. For twelve years, his cousin George—who suffered a severe head injury shortly after Dick's death and lost his memory—was mistakenly brought home to Four Winds by Captain Jim and believed by everyone, including Leslie, to be Dick Moore.

value: Dora is quiet.
unit: Dora is quiet, prim, well-behaved, and remarkably composed, remaining unruffled even during severe disruptions or emotional occasions. She is systematic, careful, neat, and industrious, diligently taking on small household tasks and studies without needing to be told twice. Though demure and sensible, her unchanging and predictable nature leads some to describe her as placid and somewhat monotonous.

label: History
value: Dora was raised alongside Davy.
unit: Dora was raised alongside her twin brother Davy under the care of a sick relative named Mary until she died, after which Marilla Cuthbert took the orphans into Green Gables with Anne Shirley's help. Unlike her mischievous brother, Dora quickly proved to be a quiet, helpful, and model child who faithfully performed her duties and memorized her Sunday lessons like a little machine. She attended school in Avonlea, where she once became terrified of going upstairs in the dark after hearing tales of a classmate's deceased uncle. As she grew older, she maintained her sensible, neat, and reliable demeanour, assisting dutifully with chores and gardening at Green Gables. On the day of Anne's wedding, fifteen-year-old Dora helped entertain Diana's young children, preparing to inherit Anne's old porch room after her departure.

label: Quotes
value: > St. George, this world would be a dull place without the men, I’ll admit, but I’m almost tempted to wish there wasn’t one of ‘em in it. Look at the trouble and bother they’ve made right here, George—torn our happy old life completely up by the roots, Saint. John Meredith began it and Norman Douglas has finished it. And now both of them have to go into limbo. Norman is the only man I ever met who agrees with me that the Kaiser of Germany is the most dangerous creature alive on this earth—and I can’t marry this sensible person because my sister is stubborn and I’m stubborner. Mark my words, St. George, the minister would come back if she raised her little finger. But she won’t George—she’ll never do it—she won’t even crook it—and I don’t dare meddle, Saint. I won’t sulk, George; Rosemary didn’t sulk, so I’m determined I won’t either, Saint; Norman will tear up the turf, but the long and short of it is, St. George, that all of us old fools must just stop thinking of marrying. Well, well, ‘despair is a free man, hope is a slave,’ Saint. So now come into the house, George, and I’ll solace you with a saucerful of cream. Then there will be one happy and contented creature on this hill at least.

label: History
value: Ellen West grew up in the West homestead on the hill.
unit: Ellen West grew up in the West homestead on the hill, living with her mother and sister Rosemary after her father and brother passed away. In her girlhood, she had a romantic relationship with Norman Douglas, which ended after a silly quarrel and led to Norman marrying someone else out of spite. Following her mother's death, Ellen and Rosemary lived quietly together for many years, bound by a mutual pledge not to marry and leave the other alone. When the minister John Meredith moved to the Glen, Ellen formed a strong friendship with him based on their shared interest in politics and world events. Later, Norman Douglas rekindled his love for Ellen after seeing her at church, and after much coaxing and persistent courtship, he arranged to marry her.

label: History
value: Faith moved from Maywater to Glen St. Mary
unit: Faith moved from Maywater to Glen St. Mary with her family, bringing along her pet rooster Adam. She befriended the Blythe children and joined them in Rainbow Valley, while also establishing the Good-Conduct Club alongside her siblings to help regulate their behavior. Due to her impulsive nature, she frequently caused local scandals, such as accidentally cleaning house and shaking rugs in the graveyard on a Sunday after confusing the days of the week, and publicizing the error in front of the entire church congregation. Determined to keep her father from being forced out of his pastorate, she successfully confronted Norman Douglas and persuaded him to return to church and pay his subscription. She tied her blue ribbon around Walter Blythe's arm prior to his fight with Dan Reese, and later formed a warm friendship with Rosemary West after confessing her grief over the death of her pet rooster.

label: Quotes
value: > Corporal punishment as a last resort is to be my rule.

label: Quotes
value: > It’s a splendid profession. A fellow has to fight something all through life . . . didn’t somebody once define man as a fighting animal? . . . and I want to fight disease and pain and ignorance . . . which are all members one of another. I want to do my share of honest, real work in the world, Anne . . . add a little to the sum of human knowledge that all the good men have been accumulating since it began. The folks who lived before me have done so much for me that I want to show my gratitude by doing something for the folks who will live after me. It seems to me that is the only way a fellow can get square with his obligations to the race.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his father
unit: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his father before returning to Avonlea, where he attended school and engaged in a prolonged academic rivalry with Anne Shirley. After attending Queen's Academy and completing Second Year work in one year, he taught school at White Sands to earn money for college, relinquishing the Avonlea school to Anne so she could remain near Green Gables. During his teaching years, he served as president of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Gilbert later attended Redmond College, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected class president, captained the Freshman football team, and ultimately graduated with High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize. Following a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he confessed his lifelong love for Anne, and they eventually married. Gilbert completed his medical training and took over the practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe, in Four Winds, before relocating his family to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary.

Moving to Prince Edward Island to live as a solitary bachelor, he bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining the Cuthbert place. He gained an immediate reputation in Avonlea as a crank who had no set meal times and harbored a strong dislike for Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Over time, he struck up a warm friendship with Anne Shirley and befriended young Davy Keith. His estranged wife Emily unexpectedly rejoined him at his Avonlea home, leading to a happy reconciliation, an improvement in his personal appearance, and regular church attendance.

value: Jane grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of Anne Shirley's close group of friends and attended Queen's Academy to study for a teaching certificate. After graduating, she taught school at Newbridge and served as a committee chairman for the Avonlea Voluntary Improvement Society. She later moved to the western prairies to teach in a school there. Eventually, she returned home and married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, remaining friendly, unspoiled by wealth, and happily devoted to her old friends.

label: Personality
value: John Meredith is shy.

He is also easily mortified and intimidated by sharp or overbearing people.

label: History
value: John Meredith served as the minister of Glen St. Mary
unit: John Meredith served as the minister of Glen St. Mary while raising his four motherless children—Jerry, Faith, Una, and Carl—at the manse. Constantly absorbed in theological reading and sermon preparations, he frequently lost track of time, forgetting meals, pastoral visits, and even parish meetings. After a harsh confrontation from Mrs. Alec Davis regarding his neglect of his children's upbringing, John was deeply shaken and sought counsel from Mrs. Blythe, realizing his personal shortcomings as a father. Around the same time, he struck up a close friendship with Walter Blythe and encountered Rosemary West at a spring in Rainbow Valley. Realizing he had fallen deeply in love with Rosemary, he eventually asked her to marry him, but received a stiff, written refusal that left him heartbroken. Despite his grief, he resolved to take up his duties alone and try to be a more attentive father to his children.

label: History
value: Josie attended Avonlea school.
unit: Josie attended Avonlea school, where she was the last member of the Pye family to be enrolled. During her school days, she showed a natural talent for walking board fences and challenged Anne Shirley to walk a ridgepole. She also participated in school concerts and events, though she sulked when she did not get her preferred role as the fairy queen. She caused a three-month quarrel with Julia Bell by making a disparaging comment about Julia's reciting bow. At the exhibition, Josie won first prize for her knitted lace. She later studied for the entrance examinations and attended Queen's Academy, taking the Second Class course for education's sake rather than out of a need to earn a living.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis was engaged to Stephen Irving in her youth.
unit: In her youth, Lavendar Lewis was engaged to Stephen Irving, but they quarreled and parted, leading him to leave for the United States. Following her mother's death ten years before Anne Shirley met her, she lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge, keeping up a tradition of hiring young Bowman girls as her sole helpers. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered her living at Echo Lodge, quickly becoming close friends and frequent visitors who shared in her imaginative play. After Stephen Irving returned and reunited with her through Anne's friendship, the couple rekindled their romance and married in late August in her honeysuckle arbor. Following their wedding, they moved to Boston along with Charlotta the Fourth and Paul Irving, where she settled into a happy domestic life.

label: History
value: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds, enduring severe family tragedies in her youth, including the death of her beloved brother Kenneth and the suicide of her father Frank West. Inheriting funds from her grandmother, she completed two years of work in one at Queen's Academy and became a teacher at Glen school. label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert spent her life living at Green Gables alongside her quiet brother, Matthew. In middle age, the siblings decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, but due to a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley was sent instead; Marilla agreed to keep her and took full charge of her upbringing. Over the years, despite her initial strictness, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne and came to view her as a daughter. Following Matthew's sudden death from heart failure, Marilla continued living at Green Gables and took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. She was overjoyed when Anne ultimately married Gilbert Blythe, the son of her former childhood beau John. In her old age, she welcomed Anne's children for visits at Green Gables, taking special delight in her grand-nephew Jem.

In middle age, the siblings decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, but due to a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley was sent instead; Marilla agreed to keep her and took full charge of her upbringing. Over the years, despite her initial strictness, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne and came to view her as a daughter. Following Matthew's sudden death from heart failure, Marilla continued living at Green Gables and took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. She was overjoyed when Anne ultimately married Gilbert Blythe, the son of her former childhood beau John. In her old age, she welcomed Anne's children for visits at Green Gables, taking special delight in her grand-nephew Jem.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was born into a family of staunch politicians.
unit: Born into a family of staunch politicians, Marshall Elliott vowed during a bitter general election fifteen years prior that he would not cut his hair or shave until his political party, the Grits, came to power. He faithfully kept his vow for fifteen years despite remaining a bachelor and looking peculiar to strangers. During this time, he spent leisure hours with local friends, such as going cod-fishing with Captain Jim and watching the old year out at the lighthouse, where he sang ballads and danced with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won power, he immediately visited the barber before sunrise to be shaved and get his hair cut. Shortly afterward, he married Miss Cornelia Bryant and lived with her for over thirteen years. He also went over-harbour to investigate the mistreatment of the child Mary Vance by Mrs. Wiley, expressing great fury over her abuse.

label: History
value: Mary Vance fled from her guardian Mrs. Wiley
unit: Mary Vance fled from her guardian Mrs. Wiley to try to reach Charlottetown, but lost her saved money and hid in an old barn in Four Winds. She was discovered there by the Meredith children, who took her into the manse kitchen and fed her. After staying temporarily at the manse, she was taken in by Cornelia Elliott (Miss Cornelia) to live in a respectable home and work in her household. Mary quickly formed close bonds with the Meredith children and the Blythe twins, spending leisure time with them in Rainbow Valley. She often taught household skills to Una Meredith, such as dishwashing and darning, but also frightened the children with gruesome tales of ghosts and blood-curdling stories about stepmothers. When Carl Meredith fell gravely ill, she was deeply distressed and cried continuously for his recovery.

value: Matthew lives at Green Gables.

value: > We’ll collaborate,” cried Owen delightedly. “You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.

value: > I’m rather glad the doctor is away,” said Owen slowly. “I wanted to see you alone, Mrs. Blythe. There is something I must tell somebody, or I think it will drive me mad. label: History
value: Owen Ford recovered from typhoid in the spring.
unit: After recovering from typhoid in the spring, Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds upon his doctor's advice to visit his grandparents' old home and seek inspiration for a novel. During his stay, he met Captain Jim Boyd and collaborated with him to write a book titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim, gathering its central material in Four Winds. While in the area, he fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore and confessed his feelings to Anne Blythe. Although he had to return to his work in Vancouver, he later returned to Four Winds to court Leslie. After their courtship, Owen and Leslie married and had children. They subsequently arranged a year-long trip to Japan so Owen could gather material for a new novel with a Japanese setting.

While in the area, he fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore and confessed his feelings to Anne Blythe. Although he had to return to his work in Vancouver, he later returned to Four Winds to court Leslie. After their courtship, Owen and Leslie married and had children. They subsequently arranged a year-long trip to Japan so Owen could gather material for a new novel with a Japanese setting.

label: History
value: Paul Irving came from Boston
unit: Paul Irving came from Boston to live with his grandmother on the shore road in Avonlea. Upon entering the local school, he instantly formed a bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized his unique genius and poetic imagination. During his school days, he befriended Lavendar Lewis, sharing fanciful stories in her garden, and inadvertently helped reunite her with his father, Stephen Irving. Following his father's remarriage to Lavendar, Paul continued his education and grew into a tall young man interested in football as well as poetry. He wrote a lyric about a bird singing at Anne's wedding that was later published in his first volume of verse. He eventually moved back to the States, where his widely published poetry inspired Anne's son, Walter Blythe.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon met Anne Shirley
unit: Philippa Gordon met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant at Redmond College and quickly became close chums with them. Coming from a rich, exclusive Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, her beauty and popularity opened doors for her friends across Redmond's social life. She struggled to choose between her suitors Alec and Alonzo until spending time at Prospect Point, where she fell in love with a minister named Jonas. She moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Stella, and Aunt Jamesina, learning household tasks while excelling in her studies. Despite initial resistance from her mother, she stood firm and married Jonas in June after graduating, eventually having children. Later, she advised Gilbert Blythe by letter that Anne was not engaged to Roy Gardner, encouraging him to try again.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant studied at Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant studied at Queen's Academy, where she formed a close circle of friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. She later worked as a schoolteacher, securing the Carmody school before taking her home school instead. During her time in Avonlea, she engaged with the local Avonlea Village Improvement Society and presented a paper on cemeteries. Later, she obtained her father's consent to attend Redmond College, where she and Anne boarded together and shared social life alongside Philippa Gordon and Stella Maynard at Patty's Place. While studying at Redmond, she focused her studies on classics. Following her graduation, Priscilla married a handsome, well-dressed foreign missionary and moved with him to Japan.

label: Personality
value: Rachel is a notable housewife.
unit: Capable, hardworking, and managing, Rachel is a notable housewife who readily attends to her own household and her neighbors' concerns. She prides herself on always speaking her mind without fear or favor and is known for being outspoken, opinionated, critical, and a meddlesome gossip. She dearly loves to be asked for advice and is a red-hot, enthusiastic Liberal politician. Despite her sharp tongue and tendency to nag, she is a kind, good Christian woman who never shirks her share of work and serves as a tender, patient nurse when caring for her sick husband.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for many years at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea with her meek husband, Thomas, keeping a sharp eye on everyone passing by. When the Cuthberts adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel criticized Anne's looks and provoked a fiery temper outburst, though she later admitted her mistake and grew fond of her. After Thomas fell ill, she served as a tender and patient nurse until his death. Following his passing, financial difficulties forced the sale of their farm, leading Rachel to accept Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables to live together. There she helped Marilla raise the twins, Davy and Dora, and tried to bring them up properly. Over the years, she traveled to Four Winds for Christmas, gifted hand-made cotton-warp quilts for Anne's wedding, and spent her old age continuing her quilt-knitting for Anne's daughters while occasionally warning Anne about household matters.

When the Cuthberts adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel criticized Anne's looks and provoked a fiery temper outburst, though she later admitted her mistake and grew fond of her. After Thomas fell ill, she served as a tender and patient nurse until his death. Following his passing, financial difficulties forced the sale of their farm, leading Rachel to accept Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables to live together. There she helped Marilla raise the twins, Davy and Dora, and tried to bring them up properly. Over the years, she traveled to Four Winds for Christmas, gifted hand-made cotton-warp quilts for Anne's wedding, and spent her old age continuing her quilt-knitting for Anne's daughters while occasionally warning Anne about household matters.

value: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College
unit: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College before studying divinity at St. Columbia. Upon graduating from St. Columbia, he took up work at a mission church on Patterson Street in the slums. Jonas married Philippa in June following his graduation. Later, the couple visited Green Gables, where Jonas offered a memorable prayer during Anne Shirley's wedding ceremony.

value: Rilla grew up at Ingleside.

label: History
value: When Rosemary was seventeen, she became engaged to Martin Crawford.
unit: When Rosemary was seventeen, she became engaged to Martin Crawford by a hidden spring in Rainbow Valley, but he drowned shortly after when his ship was wrecked. Following her mother's death and her sister Ellen's disappointment in love, Rosemary agreed to a solemn vow over her mother's Bible that neither sister would ever marry or part. She spent years living quietly with Ellen, giving music lessons to local children like Di and Nan Blythe because she enjoyed it. When John Meredith moved to the Glen, he met Rosemary and was struck by her beauty and charm, eventually falling deeply in love with her and proposing marriage. Bound by her vow to Ellen, Rosemary painfully wrote him a stiff, cool refusal to turn him away, leaving both of them heartbroken. Months later, after a visit to Kingsport, Una Meredith came to Rosemary in secret to ask her to marry her father, revealing that Mr. Meredith still loved her intensely. Rosemary welcomed Una as a friend and helper, realizing she could find happiness with John while offering love and support to his children.

value: Roy Gardner was a student at Redmond College.
unit: Roy Gardner was a student at Redmond College who had to pause his studies and travel abroad for two years to care for his sick mother. Upon returning, he actively courted Anne Shirley, sending her exotic flowers, sonnets, and exquisite letters. His romantic attentions made him widely envied and led many to expect an engagement. He introduced Anne to his mother and sisters, among whom Dorothy became a close friend of Anne. However, when he eventually expected to win her hand, Anne rejected his proposal, turning him down because she did not truly love him.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as the first female teacher in Avonlea school. She introduced innovations to the school curriculum such as alternate Friday afternoon recitations, field days in the woods to study nature, and morning and evening physical culture exercises. After catching Anne Shirley reading a novel tucked inside her Canadian history desk during school hours, Miss Stacy held her back at recess to gently correct her for wasting time and deceiving her teacher, before freely forgiving her. At the end of her first year, despite rumors that she would take a job offer in her home district's grade school, she returned to Avonlea for another term to prepare her older students for the Entrance examinations. During her tenure, she advised ambitious pupils such as Anne and Gilbert Blythe on taking up Second Year work at Queen's Academy. Her rule at Avonlea school concluded at the end of June following her second year of teaching.

label: History
value: Susan was installed as the maid-of-all-work for Gilbert and Anne Blythe
unit: Susan was installed as the maid-of-all-work for Gilbert and Anne Blythe while they lived at the little house at Four Winds. Gilbert insisted that she be kept on, and she quickly took full charge of the household duties and pantry. During her time there, she briefly left to tend to her sister Matilda, who had broken her leg. When the Blythe family moved to Ingleside, Susan relocated with them, taking charge of the household where she remained the central authority over domestic matters. She cared for the Blythe children with great devotion, taking Shirley to her brother's home for three months during his parents' absence and looking after Walter when he suffered from a toothache.

Pious and fond of prayer, she hates fighting and possesses a compassionate, sympathetic nature full of pure pity for others. Shy by nature, asking favors of people causes her great distress.

label: History
value: Una moved with her family to the Glen St. Mary manse.
unit: Una moved with her family from Maywater to the Glen St. Mary manse. She became close friends with the Ingleside children and befriended Mary Vance after helping feed and shelter her at the manse. Despite her extreme shyness, she mustered the courage to visit Mrs. Elliott to ask her to adopt Mary. Later, Mrs. Alec Davis approached her father attempting to adopt Una, but Mr. Meredith refused. Following a church incident, Una participated in a day-long fast as a punishment dictated by the Good-Conduct Club, during which she fainted from exhaustion and was rescued by Dr. Gilbert Blythe. Distressed by fear of a cruel stepmother, Una's anxiety was transformed when she overheard her father's grief over his feelings for Rosemary West; she secretly visited Rosemary to ask her to marry her father, securing Rosemary's warm promise to be a friend and helper.

Though quiet and prone to staying out of schoolboy sports and fights, he possesses an intense inner resolve when pushed to defend others.

label: History
value: Walter grows up at Ingleside.
unit: Walter grows up at Ingleside as one of the Blythe children, frequently spending his evenings playing with his siblings and companions in Rainbow Valley. Due to his quiet nature, preference for reading poetry, and avoidance of fisticuffs, he is considered 'girly' by the boys at Glen St. Mary school, though he earns a degree of respect for his eloquent way of speaking. He writes his own poetry in secret, sharing his writings only with his sister Di and looking up to 'Uncle' Paul Irving as a poetic model. After suffering from a severe toothache, he admits his deep hatred and fear of physical pain to Faith Meredith. Later, when Dan Reese insults Walter's mother, Walter overcomes his intense dread of being hurt and challenges Dan to a fight, successfully grappling with him after school while wearing Faith's blue ribbon. He also forms a close friendship with the minister, John Meredith, sharing deep talks with him in Rainbow Valley.
